claims.claim_text: For all s,t>=3, original n=(2^(s-1),1) and blue m=(2^t), sharp JOINT J=3(s+t-3)+2 and original W=3(s+t-2)+2. If both red n=(2^(s-1),1) and blue m=(2^(t-1),1) have one-edge tails, sharp JOINT J=3(s+t-3) and original W=3(s+t-2). All claims are for arbitrary finite simple host graphs, not just disjoint-star hosts. The exact proof gives a degree-two avoiding colouring below these canonical thresholds and then inducts on s using first-residual high-degree vertex and published two-component theorem for s=3. The full problem for other arbitrary nonuniform lists remains OPEN.
claims.support_summary: For Δ<=2, components are paths/cycles. Proper alternating colours of paths/even cycles yield no monochromatic P3; odd cycles yield exactly one red OR blue P3 centre. Under edge thresholds, if number k odd cycles <=r+u-2, distribute defects to cap the number of monochromatic P3 centres below target counts. If k=r+u-1, edge budget forces ALL triangle components with <=1 extra edge in red-tail/blue-uniform case, or all triangles with <=2 extra edges OR one C5 with no extras in both-tail case. Choose r triangles wholly red and the others blue, extra edges blue, or colour the C5 blue, to prevent the required additional disjoint K2 or enough P3. Therefore any arrowing original or first residual subcanonical graph has degree >=3. First residual at s=3 is the pinned full two-component size Ramsey theorem, giving sharp J. Delete an appropriate degree>=3 vertex in both residuals to reduce red component count; canonical J attained. Original host E<W has degree>=3 and every deletion has the proven sharp J, giving E>=W. Explicit complete graph-class oracle supports but is not an unbounded proof.
